The big issue is A LOT of Software Engineering jobs require a CS degree, but a CS degree doesn’t prepare you for the job. Unless you have a really and I’m mean really cool Professor that goes out their way to make leet code problems as homework and part of their curriculum and the reinforce pair programming, you won’t learn things at all. Yes you will know memory and bytes and bits and how to computational (or binary) math works, but the only language (if you have been exposed to one at all) will probably be C or C++. I have no issues with C being taught as a ton of languages are based on it, and if you want to go into game development you will most likely use C++. The issue I have is the CS major is so out of touch of reality. They don’t do market research. Like what jobs require this degree and what skills those jobs need. And literally if they let a record of what the grads are working the data would show most CS majors are just programmers. Seriously and that’s the least thing being taught in CS degree. You have more math exposure than coding. Like why ??? Come on, SQL + Python. Super versatile. Build mini games, yes. Build web apps, yes. Build scrape bots, yes. Build bots, yes. Cybersecurity, yes. Machine learning and AI, yes. Data Science, yes. And because Python is C based you can teach the basics that are similar in most languages, variables, functions, loops, conditionals, etc.. only thing differs is syntax, logic stays same. So it’s a huge disservice to the students seeing a big market for Web Development or Software Engineering and it REQUIRING A BACHELOR IN CS. They go in thinking they will come out a seasoned programmer and job ready… no they come out at square one.. yes they laid done the foundation (which took them 4 YEARS) but now they can learn ON THEIR OWN TIME THINGS THAT ACTUALLY WILL JUSTIFY OR PAY OFF THE 4 YEAR DEGREE. LITERALLY THE BIGGEST SCAM EVER… IF ALL I WANT TO DO IS DISABLE THE DISLIKE BUTTON AS A WEB DEVELOPER “SOFTWARE ENGINEER” I NEED PSYCHOLOGY, PHYSICS, CALCULUS, UNDERSTAND HOW MEMORY WORKS AND HOW THE BINARY BITS ARE ADDED AND SUBTRACTED. When in reality it’s as simple as disable={true}. AND ANOTHER DISSERVICE COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES DO, THEY DONT TEACH YOU HOW TO GOOGLE OR HOW TO STACK-OVERFLOW OR DO GIT OR VERSION CONTROL. LIKE COME ON THATS JUST PLAIN ROBBERY OF YOUR TIME, LEARNING GIT AND STACK OVERFLOW IS THE 1 MOST IMPORTANT THING IF YOU WANT TO DO ANY TUPE OF CODING. Other people ran in same problem, It’s not just you, you’re not just stupid, or sometimes it’s a know bug or side effect. For example if you put a console.log statement in useEffect hook in react causes rerenders. And you will be banging your head against the wall asking what is going on or if you did something wrong. And the answers is no and yes, you did something that you should have and that caused an an expected unexpected behavior, by unexpected I mean for you. You know nothing about clean functions yet, and etc.. You don’t know about safe practices.. And know showed you the Community on Stackoverflow, no one introduced you to the community around the language you are using, and that’s a HUGE PROBLEM. There are known bugs that you can scan for by quickly searching the libraries GitHub issues or some forum that discusses that topic, but no one taught you this, so you thing youre alone and you caused this issue and you’re dumb and it’s you and you want to give up because you don’t understand why something is happening or producing a weird side effect. And I guess Unis and colleges do it to weed out people and only get the people that are “smart” and willing to put in the work and effort. But come on seriously why overcomplicate things for beginners that are taking their first CS class ? Use an easy syntax language like Python to introduce basics and CS concepts and basic Algorithm structure. Then in more advanced classes move on to Java or C++ or still over advanced in Python. There is absolutely no need to do basic CS intro class in C other than the fact that that’s how it was we suffered no you suffer. Or because that’s the professor weird obsession language. And im not dogging and all teachers. I had great professors. Some ecoraged us to explore beyond the covered curriculum, for example for a JS (vanilla JS) class my professor accepted work in REACT JS, I even submitted some work in Typescript and he was super stoked about it. And I had teachers that made us do a ton of programming, pair up with partners for the whole semester to do weekly challenges and also you have to do your own side quest challenge. But then again I had professors who hand you the book listed what to read and what exercises to do from the book, left for the entire semester ( online class) no lectures no check ins, due date on all assignments was last day of class. Absolute dumpster fire of a class. And some teachers are so lazy they reuse and recycle their old material it so reused you can find other students work or notes online.. So then you’re both putting as minimal effort as possible to seem as you’re working and none of you will admit that you’re not so you will pass with at least a C. Just know what you’re getting yourself into and why ?? Be mindful of what you will learn and questions things always and research and learn constantly, only way you will survive.

Sorry Jason, but this is just misinformation. Your analogy fails because you're not just CONSUMING the food (that's the users), you are MAKING the food (that's the developers). Even Robert "Uncle Bob" Martin, who said he doesn't even glance at the generated code, specifically said that new developers "Shouldn't even look at Agents for the first THREE years of their career" and that to be able to properly develop real taste and understanding, you need "20-30 years, and make a lot of mistakes". Expertise and mastery don't happen purely through observation and dialogue, but through experience, repetition, and trial and error; you have to fail to succeed. If I wanted to learn how to cook, I could watch a Master Chef work and make endless inquiries. After a month, I would be able to describe the perfectly medium-rare ribeye but never know what it's like to cook one, and I'd almost certainly overcook it on my first attempt.
